This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars.

entries.capability_summary: account-pool (community, maintained by roqianjas) Run several accounts of one provider in Hermes' credential pool: `hermes account <provider> <action>` adds accounts with email verification, shows live usage per account, keeps the least-used account first (fill_first + a 5-minute balance timer over every provider with accounts), parks accounts for hours or on a weekly schedule, shows which bot is on which account and its tokens at API prices, alerts on dead logins, a full pool or a runaway bot, and can start an idle account's 5-hour window with one tiny request (wake). Adapters for anthropic and openai-codex; generic commands for any pool provider. Optional Accounts page in Hermes Desktop. Linux and Windows. Disclosure — logins stay in Hermes: park holds an entry out of rotation in Hermes' pool (mark_exhausted_and_rotate, reason "parked") and unpark is reset_status; the plugin's park list holds labels, ids and times only; expired tokens are refreshed by Hermes (try_refresh_matching); sign-in, in the terminal and on the Desktop page, runs `hermes auth add`; other profiles' accounts are read with read_credential_pool. It uses each account's access token as Hermes stores it for live usage and the email check (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and /profile, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, with the client headers of Hermes' usage fetcher) and for wake (a command, a page button, or the timer after the opt-in `wake auto-on`): one one-word request per account through Hermes' Anthropic client or the Codex Responses endpoint, and the account's model list. Telegram alerts through `hermes send -t telegram` to the bot's home channel or a chat id kept in account-pool.json; no telemetry. Its session tracker, a post_api_request hook, runs in every profile and writes labels, ids and token counts only. `setup` writes plugins.enabled of every profile, links the plugin into every profile, removes the retired account-pool-tracker (`hermes plugins remove`) and, with --timer, adds a systemd user timer (Linux) or a Task Scheduler task for the user (Windows, no admin rights). Runs systemctl --user and notify-send (Linux), schtasks, powershell.exe and taskkill (Windows), hermes config set, hermes auth add/remove, hermes send, hermes plugins remove; reads every profile's config.yaml and state.db (read-only), the gateway config (whether the Telegram bot has a home channel) and /proc on Linux. The command registers in the default profile only and provides no tools. Live usage, the email check and wake send each account's own access token from Hermes' pool straight to its vendor with Claude Code (anthropic) and Codex CLI (openai-codex) client headers. The session tracker reads the running agent's current pool account (label and id only) by scanning Python thread frames for Hermes' private _credential_pool. On the first run after 3.x it moves parked logins from account-pool-parked.json back into Hermes' pool and deletes that file. This plugin hook(s): post_api_request. Platforms: linux, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6. Known issues: After installing, run `hermes account <provider> setup` (add --timer for the 5-minute balance timer): it lists the plugin in every profile for the Desktop page and links it into every profile for the session tracker. Coming from 3.x it also removes account-pool-tracker.; Hermes can let a parked account back into rotation early (`hermes auth reset`, or a Codex quota it sees come back); the next balance run parks it again, and doctor names it until then. A park without --until is held for 30 days, and a balance run renews it once less than 15 days are left, so without the timer it ends after 30 days.; Windows: tested with a stand-in Task Scheduler and, up to 3.13, with Windows' own Python, cmd.exe and wscript.exe under Wine; not yet on a Windows machine. On Windows the timer runs only while the user is signed in.; Built for plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under host, Hermes skips plugin CLI commands, so `hermes account` and the timer's balance are unavailable.; Usage comes from undocumented provider endpoints (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage) that can change or rate-limit without notice; bots are unaffected when they do.; The Desktop page's sign-in relays `hermes auth add` and has run in sandbox tests (Hermes' real sign-in code, provider calls replaced), not yet with a new account on a real install. The Codex browser sign-in needs the browser on the same computer; when port 1455 is taken, Hermes signs in with a device code instead..

entries.capability_summary: agent-batch (community, maintained by raaaas) Parallel AI task orchestrator. Paste a task list into the desktop panel; Hermes phases it into dependency-ordered groups through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools (or you group it yourself in one click), then each phase dispatches one independent coding agent per task to a GitHub Actions workflow in a repo you name — own branch, own PR — and the panel tracks the runs and the PRs. GITHUB_TOKEN is the only required credential; AGENT_BATCH_REPO, AGENT_BATCH_WORKFLOW, AGENT_BATCH_MODEL and AGENT_BATCH_STATE are optional (the last is a directory override for the plan file, not a secret) and each can be set per plan in the panel instead. Disclosure — Hermes can read and rewrite the stored phase plan through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools, but dispatch is always a confirmed click in the panel. Each dispatch fires a GitHub workflow_dispatch with your GITHUB_TOKEN (Actions + pull-requests write) on the repo you name. The workflow you copy into that repo installs third-party coding-agent CLIs (cline by default; the others are unpinned npm packages) and runs them unattended, with auto-approve / skip-permissions, repo write access and your provider secrets. They push real branches and open real PRs, and your task text and repository code go to that runner's model vendor. LLM cost belongs to the runner: cline spends Cline Credits or a BYOK key, opencode free models need its zen relay, kilo needs an active Kilo Go subscription (keyless CI runs fail), and claude-code / codex / dsh need their own keys. This plugin registers tool(s): agent_batch_plan, agent_batch_phase; requires env var(s): GITHUB_TOKEN. Requires Hermes >=0.21.3.

entries.capability_summary: agent-hint (community, maintained by dachaimahogany) Give the inference engine behind each request a standard, machine-readable view of the agent session that produced it. Injects an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON: session identity and call index, lifecycle state, soft priority, a cache-pinning hint, optional measured statistics) on main LLM requests, and can emit session lifecycle events out of band as local ndjson or as POSTs to a URL you configure. Request bodies are never modified, and nothing is added or sent until the plugin is enabled. Lets a scheduler pin a session to the instance already holding its KV cache, or rank a user-blocked session above background work, without teaching the engine anything about the client. Disclosure — when enabled, every main LLM request carries an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON with the session id, call index, lifecycle state, priority and cache hints) to whatever provider is configured, not only hint-aware engines; with status_sink: http the same session events and usage/latency statistics are POSTed to the status_url you set, and ndjson writes them under $HERMES_HOME. This plugin hook(s): on_session_start, on_session_end, on_session_finalize, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_approval_request, post_approval_response, subagent_start, subagent_stop, post_api_request; middleware: llm_request. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: agent-janitor (community, maintained by ZidoCode) Process hygiene for agent machines — finds the background processes your agent left behind (dev servers, tunnels, watchers, nohup jobs) using evidence signals (ppid=1 reparent, port listener via /proc/net/tcp{,6}, dev-server traits, TTL exceeded) and attributes them to the originating tool call via agent-ledger's ledger when present. Dry-run by default: nothing is killed until you write policy_mode=enforce; system daemons and host/VM management agents are exempt by name, a user-editable whitelist covers your real infrastructure, and each kill re-reads the cmdline first (SIGTERM, 2s, SIGKILL with PID-reuse check). stdlib-only, fails open. Disclosure — inside Hermes it only appends terminal commands that look like they start background work (first 300 characters, which can include inline secrets) to plugin-data/agent-janitor/spawns.jsonl, and reads agent-ledger's ledger.db read-only when present. Killing is a separate CLI you run yourself (janitor_cli.py sweep): after you write "enforce" to plugin-data/agent-janitor/policy_mode it sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL to every process re-parented to PID 1 for over a minute that is not on its built-in exempt list or your whitelist, whoever started it (for example a tmux server or a nohup'd hermes gateway), including other users' processes when run as root. Dry-run first; the dry-run list is the kill list. This plugin hook(s): post_tool_call. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: agora (community, maintained by yzy806806) Self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a real Hermes profile with its own SOUL.md and skills; they discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A "leader" profile chairs the discussions and a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase. Discussion and execution share one board: a motion is a sub-task of a per-project team channel task, speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` comments, the conclusion is written to task.result, and an adopted conclusion becomes execution tasks parented to the motion so context reaches workers through Hermes' own parent handoff. Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks, a dashboard tab and an `hermes agora` CLI; installing writes nothing — the three bundled skills are deployed by an explicit `hermes agora setup`. Disclosure — creates a Hermes profile per worker by asking core to provision it (`hermes profile create --clone`, which copies config.yaml and .env into the new profile as owner-only files, never symlinks to the real credentials); spawns `hermes -p <profile> chat -Q -q` subprocesses to speak in discussions and to run dispatched tasks, which execute as full agents with that profile's toolset, including terminal and file writes inside the project workdir. Those subprocesses receive `--yolo --accept-hooks` ONLY when the project opted in via `agora_start_project(allow_unattended=True)`; the default is off, so a freshly installed team can read, discuss and plan but its flagged writes and shell commands fail closed. Also reads and writes the kanban database (tasks, task_comments, task_events, task_runs, task_links) restricted to its own project boards, including a persistent team-channel task pinned in `scheduled` status, and deletes a project's own tasks when it stops or completes; registers one recurring cron job and writes its runner script to HERMES_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh; writes AGENTS.md into the configured project workdir; deploys three bundled skills into HERMES_HOME/skills/collaboration/; and serves a dashboard tab plus REST routes through the Hermes dashboard. No network egress of its own — model calls happen inside the spawned Hermes subprocesses under the operator's own provider credentials. This plugin registers tool(s): agora_start_project, agora_stop_project, agora_project_status, agora_update_project, agora_create_task, agora_close_task, agora_raise_motion, agora_get_messages, agora_get_result, agora_list_motions, agora_close_motion, agora_message, agora_read_chat, agora_create_worker, agora_list_workers, agora_remove_worker, agora_list_templates, agora_create_team, agora_list_teams, agora_remove_team; hook(s): kanban_task_completed, kanban_task_claimed, kanban_task_blocked. Requires Hermes >=0.20.

entries.capability_summary: alans-way-computer (community, maintained by capthvnsen) Computer-use provider for Hermes: the stock computer_use tool drives desktop apps on the user's computer through the Alan's Workspace app, and on the VM's own desktop when the computer is offline. Needs the Alan's Way Plugin's workspace setup. Select it with computer_use.backend: alans-way-computer (the Alan's Way Plugin's setup.sh sets this when it installs the provider; in the catalog flow it prints the command). Disclosure — starts the workspace router from the profile's mcp_servers.workspace_browser block (command and args from config.yaml, with a filtered environment plus HERMES_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_DESKTOP_ACTIONS=1, which lets this private router child serve desktop input) as a long-running node child per session. The filtered environment passes PATH, HOME, locale and OS basics, plus DISPLAY, XAUTHORITY and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS so the router's VM-desktop fallback finds the X display and session bus; no keys or tokens. It talks to the router over stdio (app lists, element trees, screenshots and input actions). The router reaches the user's computer over SSH on the user's tailnet and falls back to the VM's desktop, where it uses xdotool, a screenshot tool and the AT-SPI accessibility bus if they are installed (the provider installs none of them). The provider never takes the focused window on the user's computer, and every input action still goes through Hermes's computer_use approval gate (cua:*:background entries in command_allowlist, which the Alan's Way Plugin's --allow-desktop-actions adds, skip the prompt). The provider itself makes no network calls. On Hermes 0.21.5, which has no provider API, it installs and does nothing. Since 0.21.0, captures keep element numbers stable across action replies on Mac and Windows, fold in changed controls and report removed numbers; a truncated list never treats unseen controls as removed. Linux keeps the whole-tree generation guard, so capture again before acting by number after a change. Action replies describe nearby changes and can mark the effect confirmed. Default som captures still fetch a screenshot to measure the window, but omit it from the model when named controls cover at least 35%; mode vision explicitly includes it and mode ax requests no screenshot. Replies identify the coordinate space and explain locked screens, missing permissions, unreadable or cut trees, hung apps and uncertain outcomes before a retry. Element trees, generation, screenshots' geometry and host OS are session memory, with no new persistent provider state, tools, hooks, middleware, required environment variables or direct network destinations. Browser commit approvals are separate from this provider's unchanged computer_use approval gate. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: Needs a Hermes build with the pluggable computer-use API (merged to main after 0.21.5). On older Hermes the plugin installs and does nothing. Install alans-way first and run its workspace setup, which writes the workspace_browser block this provider reuses.; Hermes asks for approval on every computer_use action type until it is granted. For an unattended Telegram bot, grant them once with Always in Telegram, or add cua:<action>:background entries to command_allowlist (see the README). Takes effect after a gateway restart.; Runs only in the plugin host: it cannot load under plugins.isolation: host, because the provider hands Hermes a live router session.; Typing without a target field works only on the VM's own desktop, where it types at the focused window (still approval-gated). On the user's computer the app never takes focus, so the agent uses set_value on a field instead.; The VM desktop path needs xdotool, a screenshot tool (scrot, maim or ImageMagick import), the AT-SPI bus and python3-gi on the VM. Without them those calls fail and the agent reports it; setup.sh warns about what is missing.; A default som capture may fetch the window screenshot even when it is omitted from the model after the 35% coverage check. Use mode vision to request it explicitly, or mode ax for an element-only capture. When a screenshot is omitted, coordinate= and element bounds are screen pixels.; Mac and Windows action replies update the held element list without shifting surviving numbers. On Linux, capture again before acting by number after a tree change; cut replies do not prove an unseen control is gone. A timeout or hung app can leave the action's outcome uncertain: capture before retrying..

entries.capability_summary: alans-way (community, maintained by capthvnsen) Idle check-ins from the primary bot of a Hermes gateway on a Linux machine or a macOS guest VM: when the bound Telegram chat has been quiet for two hours, during 08:00-22:00 in the user's timezone, the bot checks in once (does one safe step and reports it, suggests one, or asks one question), backing off when unanswered. The model tool can only make check-ins quieter; more often, resume and wider hours are operator-only via /proactivity or the CLI. After install, the workspace-setup skill walks the agent through setting up Alan's Workspace (a separate desktop app for the user's computer: macOS or Windows) and Tailscale; desktop input goes only through Hermes's approval-gated computer_use tool. Disclosure — once the gateway connects Telegram, a background thread checks every 60 seconds. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, doubling per unanswered check-in, 08:00-22:00 user time), it injects an internal user-role prompt into that chat (needs plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection, which setup sets), so the bot runs a turn on its own and may take one "safe, reversible" step; the user still approves tool calls in Telegram. Its pre_llm_call/post_llm_call hooks see every session's turns and store only the bound chat's timestamps in plugin state. On first load it reads $HERMES_HOME/companion/proactivity/proactivity.sqlite3 once, read-only. The plugin itself makes no network calls. The workspace-setup skill has the agent fetch this repo at the catalog pin into ~/alans-way-agents (or reuse a clean clone there) and run setup.sh, which does the following. (1) Installs long-running services (Alan's Tools: a managed Chrome/Chromium on a loopback-only debugging port, the first free port from 9223 up, plus a browser broker and an optional availability watcher): systemd units hermes-alans-way-chromium, -browser and mac-watch with loginctl enable-linger where systemd is running; supervisord programs alans-way-chromium, alans-way-browser and alans-way-mac-watch, written to a conf.d file, where it is not (VM images and containers); a KeepAlive LaunchAgent on a macOS guest; logon Scheduled Tasks on Windows. When no X display is running it also installs and runs Xvfb on :99 (unit hermes-alans-way-xvfb or program alans-way-xvfb, -nolisten tcp). (2) Installs packages when they are missing, only as root or with passwordless sudo, through apt, dnf or yum: Google Chrome stable (the current .deb downloaded from dl.google.com on amd64 apt hosts, which also adds Google's apt repository, so the host keeps taking Chrome updates from Google), else the distro chromium package, else Playwright 1.49.1 Chromium through npx (root only); and xvfb. It only warns, and installs nothing, for xdotool, scrot, at-spi2-core and python3-gi, which the VM desktop path needs. (3) Appends the user's computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (administrators_authorized_keys on a Windows admin account) with a from= restriction to the Tailscale ranges 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rewriting an existing unrestricted line for the same key; pins its host key in known_hosts and adds a ControlMaster block to ~/.ssh/config for Tailscale hosts only (with a tailscale nc ProxyCommand when Tailscale runs in userspace-networking mode). (4) Adds a TimeoutStartSec=180 drop-in to the hermes-gateway unit. Hermes refuses plugin file changes while a gateway is running, so setup drain-stops that profile's gateway (SIGUSR1 under supervisord, else systemctl stop or hermes gateway stop), replays the refused plugin install or update, and starts it again. With --restart it restarts the gateway only if setup changed something the gateway loads (or an earlier restart never happened), detached about ten seconds after printing its summary: by SIGUSR1 drain under supervisord, else a transient systemd-run timer or hermes gateway restart. (5) For the main profile and every profile with its own Telegram bot, writes a managed mcp_servers.workspace_browser block (removing other entries that run this router, with a backup; a re-run keeps the computer address and OS it already holds, and --mac-ssh none removes them), turns off the built-in browser toolset for Telegram and cron (--keep-browser leaves it on), turns computer_use on for Telegram and cron, and sets computer_use.backend to alans-way-computer when it installed or found that provider (under the skill's --skip-plugin flow it only warns and prints the config command). It reads each profile's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN only to derive the numeric bot id. It warns, and changes nothing, when a copy of the workspace-operations skill in a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's. The workspace router reaches the user's computer over SSH on their tailnet; on the user's computer it calls the local API of Alan's Workspace on 127.0.0.1 with that app's bearer token. The existing proactivity tool may disable the brief but cannot enable it; settings.morning_brief and last_brief_date are stored in the existing idle plugin state. It checks control names, selectors, refs, action-looking URLs, batches, scripts, keys and dialogs against page state; missing page knowledge needs a snapshot or explicit commit. Shared commit-name patterns allow benign Buy it again, Book a demo and Subscribe & Save labels without excusing other commit-bearing words. An approved commit is never replayed after a lost connection or host change. It appends commit decisions to commit-decisions.jsonl beside the mac-watch state file, creating the log with mode 0600: timestamp, bot id, page origin, decision and any supplied kind, summary, amount, currency and counterparty, or the detected target. Page/control/challenge and pending-approval state is held in memory. The check-in menu now ends with asking about a decision the user owns. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing, and neither setup script writes any of these keys. When the VNC viewer binds loopback only, the skill can, with explicit consent, have the human run a temporary SSH forward to the computer's loopback (local port 16080, ends after 30 minutes) and verify it with curl from that computer. For a manual or file install it explains the Hermes scanner result and, only after explicit consent to the exact reviewed revision, may retry hermes plugins install with --ref SHA --enable --force; --force confirms a caution verdict and cannot override a dangerous one. If the plugin is already installed from the catalog, setup leaves it as it is, so this pin stays.; Setup turns off Hermes's stock browser toolset for Telegram and cron so the agent uses the workspace browser (pass --keep-browser to leave it on). A background thread checks every 60 seconds once the gateway connects Telegram.; Setup may install Chrome, Chromium, Playwright's Chromium or Xvfb with root or passwordless sudo, and may drain-stop and start the profile's gateway to apply a plugin change Hermes refuses while it runs. Pass --skip-services to skip the services and their packages.; The computer's SSH key is only accepted from the tailnet (from= restriction). An existing unrestricted line for the same key is rewritten with it.; A copy of the workspace-operations skill under a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's and never gets its updates. Setup only warns; move anything worth keeping out of it, then delete it.; The Telegram texting voice is on by default in every enabled profile. /tone default turns off its note and final-reply polish; check-ins and morning briefs keep their own short style. Without MCP form elicitation support commits fail with approval_unavailable; unattended cron declines them. The gate protects against agent mistakes and malicious pages, not a deliberately hostile bot with same-user terminal/file access.; The router appends approval details and detected targets to commit-decisions.jsonl beside mac-watch state, shared by routers using that path; no retention or rotation is implemented. Keep this local log private. CAPTCHA handback, recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still block takeover. If the router reports human_has_control before a commit approval, wait or claim the tab through the normal app control flow first.; Long-chat pruning is an agent-guided, separately consented config option per profile, not a setup.sh default. It preserves customized values and summary routing, rewrites sent history and can break the prompt-cache prefix; undo affects future pruning and cannot restore tool bodies already pruned from active context.; web-errands and integrations are agent guidance, not setup steps. Any Himalaya, rclone, Taskwarrior, Home Assistant or Honcho install happens only after the user agrees in chat, never from setup.sh or plugin load. Taskwarrior is built from source (CMake >=3.24, Rust >=1.91.1 and several GiB of temporary space). The Google Workspace route requests Hermes's fixed scope list, which includes write access.; Guided setup can change a profile's busy-input, Telegram display, notification, reaction, memory-notice, cron-wrapping and timezone settings, but only after explicit answers. Busy mode, memory-notice hiding, cron.wrap_response and timezone reach beyond Telegram within that profile. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing; neither setup script writes these keys.; setup.sh --bind also sets TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL for the bound profile through hermes config set and clears TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID; it loads on gateway restart. If that fails, send /sethome in the primary DM.; Desktop control needs a Hermes with tools.computer_use.backend.ComputerUseProvider (commit 63f5e0ea45726c5d8d7d207d140613997730aab3 or newer); a version string alone does not prove it. setup.sh --verify exits 2, not 0, for a partial install..
entries.description: Idle check-ins from the primary bot of a Hermes gateway on a Linux machine or a macOS guest VM: when the bound Telegram chat has been quiet for two hours, during 08:00-22:00 in the user's timezone, the bot checks in once (does one safe step and reports it, suggests one, or asks one question), backing off when unanswered. The model tool can only make check-ins quieter; more often, resume and wider hours are operator-only via /proactivity or the CLI. After install, the workspace-setup skill walks the agent through setting up Alan's Workspace (a separate desktop app for the user's computer: macOS or Windows) and Tailscale; desktop input goes only through Hermes's approval-gated computer_use tool. Disclosure — once the gateway connects Telegram, a background thread checks every 60 seconds. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, doubling per unanswered check-in, 08:00-22:00 user time), it injects an internal user-role prompt into that chat (needs plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection, which setup sets), so the bot runs a turn on its own and may take one "safe, reversible" step; the user still approves tool calls in Telegram. Its pre_llm_call/post_llm_call hooks see every session's turns and store only the bound chat's timestamps in plugin state. On first load it reads $HERMES_HOME/companion/proactivity/proactivity.sqlite3 once, read-only. The plugin itself makes no network calls. The workspace-setup skill has the agent fetch this repo at the catalog pin into ~/alans-way-agents (or reuse a clean clone there) and run setup.sh, which does the following. (1) Installs long-running services (Alan's Tools: a managed Chrome/Chromium on a loopback-only debugging port, the first free port from 9223 up, plus a browser broker and an optional availability watcher): systemd units hermes-alans-way-chromium, -browser and mac-watch with loginctl enable-linger where systemd is running; supervisord programs alans-way-chromium, alans-way-browser and alans-way-mac-watch, written to a conf.d file, where it is not (VM images and containers); a KeepAlive LaunchAgent on a macOS guest; logon Scheduled Tasks on Windows. When no X display is running it also installs and runs Xvfb on :99 (unit hermes-alans-way-xvfb or program alans-way-xvfb, -nolisten tcp). (2) Installs packages when they are missing, only as root or with passwordless sudo, through apt, dnf or yum: Google Chrome stable (the current .deb downloaded from dl.google.com on amd64 apt hosts, which also adds Google's apt repository, so the host keeps taking Chrome updates from Google), else the distro chromium package, else Playwright 1.49.1 Chromium through npx (root only); and xvfb. It only warns, and installs nothing, for xdotool, scrot, at-spi2-core and python3-gi, which the VM desktop path needs. (3) Appends the user's computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (administrators_authorized_keys on a Windows admin account) with a from= restriction to the Tailscale ranges 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rewriting an existing unrestricted line for the same key; pins its host key in known_hosts and adds a ControlMaster block to ~/.ssh/config for Tailscale hosts only (with a tailscale nc ProxyCommand when Tailscale runs in userspace-networking mode). (4) Adds a TimeoutStartSec=180 drop-in to the hermes-gateway unit. Hermes refuses plugin file changes while a gateway is running, so setup drain-stops that profile's gateway (SIGUSR1 under supervisord, else systemctl stop or hermes gateway stop), replays the refused plugin install or update, and starts it again. With --restart it restarts the gateway only if setup changed something the gateway loads (or an earlier restart never happened), detached about ten seconds after printing its summary: by SIGUSR1 drain under supervisord, else a transient systemd-run timer or hermes gateway restart. The setup skill also offers, each only after an explicit answer, with readback and a remembered-choice marker in the profile's config: display.busy_input_mode (steer or interrupt, for every platform in that profile; asked once, only when the effective mode is interrupt and no choice is recorded) and one grouped Telegram question covering platforms.telegram.typing_indicator, display.platforms.telegram.interim_assistant_messages, tool_progress, notifications, long_running_notifications and busy_steer_ack_enabled, platforms.telegram.reactions, display.memory_notifications (hides the Memory updated and Self-improvement review notices on every platform in that profile), cron.wrap_response (profile-wide: removes scheduled-message headers, job IDs and footers for all delivery targets) and, as a separate city-confirmed question, timezone. Markers written through the same CLI are skills.config.workspace-setup.busy_input_choice and telegram_feel_choice; a legacy busy_steer_ack_choice marker is only read, never written. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing, and neither setup script writes any of these keys. When the VNC viewer binds loopback only, the skill can, with explicit consent, have the human run a temporary SSH forward to the computer's loopback (local port 16080, ends after 30 minutes) and verify it with curl from that computer. For a manual or file install it explains the Hermes scanner result and, only after explicit consent to the exact reviewed revision, may retry hermes plugins install with --ref SHA --enable --force; --force confirms a caution verdict and cannot override a dangerous one. Hermes's unmodified scanner reports SAFE for this plugin: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python_subprocess: the two git helpers in skills/workspace-setup/SKILL.md) and 3 LOW (hardcoded_ip_port: the loopback forward examples in the same file).
known_issues: Install this on the machine that runs Hermes (a Linux host or a macOS guest VM), not on the user's primary computer. Windows guests are new and untested on real hardware. If the plugin is already installed from the catalog, setup leaves it as it is, so this pin stays.

Setup turns off Hermes's stock browser toolset for Telegram and cron so the agent uses the workspace browser (pass --keep-browser to leave it on). It never turns off computer_use: on Hermes with the computer-use provider API, desktop input goes through the gated computer_use tool and its alans-way-computer provider.
Check-ins need plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection: true and a bound Telegram DM (setup does both). A background thread checks every 60 seconds once the gateway connects Telegram.

Setup may install Chrome, Chromium, Playwright's Chromium or Xvfb with root or passwordless sudo, and may drain-stop and start the profile's gateway to apply a plugin change Hermes refuses while it runs. Pass --skip-services to skip the services and their packages.
The computer's SSH key is only accepted from the tailnet (from= restriction). An existing unrestricted line for the same key is rewritten with it.
A copy of the workspace-operations skill under a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's and never gets its updates. Setup only warns; move anything worth keeping out of it, then delete it.

The Telegram texting voice is on by default in every enabled profile. /tone default turns off its note and final-reply polish; check-ins and morning briefs keep their own short style. Fixed Hermes approval/error/progress messages, direct sends and cron reports are outside these hooks; interim messages get the tone note but no polish, and streaming may show raw chunks before the final edit.

Morning briefs are opt-in (/proactivity brief on), use the existing bound DM and gateway-injection permission, and may read calendar/email through tools already available to the model. /proactivity now is user-only from that chat and bypasses pause/hours for one requested check-in.

Telegram browser Approve buttons need Hermes v0.21.6 or newer including commit 239740a19e (first in date tag v2026.6.19), despite the generic >=0.21.5 install floor. Without MCP form elicitation support commits fail with approval_unavailable; unattended cron declines them. The gate protects against agent mistakes and malicious pages, not a deliberately hostile bot with same-user terminal/file access.

The router appends approval details and detected targets to commit-decisions.jsonl beside mac-watch state, shared by routers using that path; no retention or rotation is implemented. Keep this local log private. CAPTCHA handback, recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still block takeover. If the router reports human_has_control before a commit approval, wait or claim the tab through the normal app control flow first.

Long-chat pruning is an agent-guided, separately consented config option per profile, not a setup.sh default. It preserves customized values and summary routing, rewrites sent history and can break the prompt-cache prefix; undo affects future pruning and cannot restore tool bodies already pruned from active context.

web-errands and integrations are agent guidance, not setup steps. Any Himalaya, rclone, Taskwarrior, Home Assistant or Honcho install happens only after the user agrees in chat, never from setup.sh or plugin load. Taskwarrior is built from source (CMake >=3.24, Rust >=1.91.1 and several GiB of temporary space). The Google Workspace route requests Hermes's fixed scope list, which includes write access.

Guided setup can change a profile's busy-input, Telegram display, notification, reaction, memory-notice, cron-wrapping and timezone settings, but only after explicit answers. Busy mode, memory-notice hiding, cron.wrap_response and timezone reach beyond Telegram within that profile. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing; neither setup script writes these keys.

setup.sh --bind also sets TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL for the bound profile through hermes config set and clears TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID; it loads on gateway restart. If that fails, send /sethome in the primary DM.

Desktop control needs a Hermes with tools.computer_use.backend.ComputerUseProvider (commit 63f5e0ea45726c5d8d7d207d140613997730aab3 or newer); a version string alone does not prove it. setup.sh --verify exits 2, not 0, for a partial install.

entries.capability_summary: alice-voice (community, maintained by bablobanov) Private Yandex Alice voice input for Hermes, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL. This plugin requires env var(s): ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.21.3. Known issues: Default profile and one existing authorized Telegram DM session only; a private Alice skill and operator-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy are required.; Requires in-process plugin execution: the Telegram connect factory receives the native Application and is not supported by plugins.isolation: host.; The webhook URL contains a bearer secret. Yandex request signatures are not verified; body skill/account IDs are not cryptographic authentication.; Alice acknowledges asynchronous scheduling, not completion or delivery. Replies are sent to Telegram, not spoken by Alice.; Deduplication is bounded and memory-only; no durable queue, exactly-once guarantee, or built-in global rate limiter..

entries.capability_summary: antigravity-oauth (community, maintained by neerazz) Sign in to Google Antigravity with `hermes auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx hermes-antigravity-oauth`) and run Hermes on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your Hermes SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching Hermes tool, which then runs under Hermes approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). entries.capability_summary: artifacts (community, maintained by dmmeteo) Private library for the finished documents agents make (self-contained HTML, Markdown, SVG, PNG, WebP), with an Artifacts dashboard tab and explicit, expiring, revocable guest links for one artifact each. Early public preview. Disclosure — the plugin is a client of a separate Artifacts service you run yourself from the same repository (not installed by the plugin): six tools and the dashboard tab send artifact bytes and metadata to HERMES_ARTIFACTS_URL with the machine credential HERMES_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN, resolved through Hermes secret scope, held server-side and never sent to the browser. artifact_publish reads a resolved local path only after Hermes read-policy and supported-extension checks; an explicit kind must match. artifact_download checks raw and resolved destinations against Hermes write policy, refuses approval-required paths even with overwrite=true, and writes atomically through a temporary sibling. File policy is defense in depth, not filesystem isolation. Sharing creates a public bearer link on your service; revocation cannot recall copies. Stores no data and no credentials of its own; no hooks, background processes or telemetry. This plugin registers tool(s): artifact_publish, artifact_list, artifact_get, artifact_download, artifact_share, artifact_revoke_share; requires env var(s): HERMES_ARTIFACTS_URL, HERMES_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: Conflicts with artifact-relay because both register artifact_publish. Enable only one of these plugins.; Needs the Hermes Artifacts service running separately (run from source; no package or image yet). Tested with Hermes 0.21.x and in Chromium only..

entries.capability_summary: author-feed (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Read one public profile and watch one account, with profile_get, author_feed and author_watch. Disclosure — HTTPS GET only to public.api.bsky.app, no API key, and no program on your machine. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. hermes author-feed schedule creates one cron job, a model turn every hour by default (two or more model requests, no daily cap). Delivered to local unless you pass --deliver, so no chat by default. Run hermes author-feed unschedule before removal. A leftover job after the plugin is gone stops with hermes cron remove <id>. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private Hermes parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall. This plugin registers tool(s): profile_get, author_feed, author_watch. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: biomimetic-brain (community, maintained by ousiaresearch) Meters and a gate for a long-running agent — 25 subsystem state files (energy, fatigue, circadian phase, motivation, novelty, attention, conflict, values, open questions), one folded brain-state.json the rest of the agent reads, four maintenance passes that keep it honest, and a read-only PROCEED / CAUTION / VETO decision gate whose refusals name the numbers behind them. Provides the mind-kit skill, which seeds the files, produces the aggregate, schedules the passes and teaches the gate. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND_AGENT_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars.

entries.capability_summary: blackbox (community, maintained by Umanitek) Security for agents: checks every tool call and model request before it runs against a curated, verifiable threat graph (prompt injection, dangerous commands, malicious packages, unsafe skills, phishing and drainer indicators) and local rules that keep an agent away from wallet stores, seed phrases, private keys and exchange API keys. Audit mode records; block mode refuses. Can share privacy-safe threat reports with an open community graph once the user turns sharing on (off by default); community findings only ever flag. Hooks only: no tools, no middleware. Disclosure — hooks see every tool call and model request; `hermes blackbox setup` installs Node (via a checksum-pinned nvm installer) if missing, the OriginTrail DKG node from npm (checksum-pinned) and Blazegraph in Docker or Oxigraph, registers the DKG node and the dashboard as login services (systemd/LaunchAgent), and joins the DKG peer-to-peer network; package installs are looked up on api.osv.dev (name and version); community threat reports signed by a local reporter key (threat identifiers, including domains of fetched pages that served a verified injection) are shared to the community graph only after you turn sharing on (off by default); the optional LLM reviewer sends the current turn's user and tool text to OpenAI or Anthropic; `blackbox attach` copies the plugin into the Hermes homes/profiles and OpenClaw workspaces you name and enables it in their config (automatic attaching is off unless you set `auto_attach: true`); `hermes blackbox chat` creates an `agent-blackbox` profile cloned from the current one (config.yaml and .env); the dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9700. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_api_request, on_session_start, on_session_end. Requires Hermes >=0.21.7. Known issues: After installing, run `hermes blackbox setup` once: it installs Blackbox's local DKG node (a pinned, checksum-verified OriginTrail release from npm) and its graph store (Blazegraph in Docker, or Oxigraph when Docker is not available), then syncs the verified threat graph. Until setup has run, the built-in rules protect and `hermes blackbox status` says setup is needed..

entries.capability_summary: boardstate (community, maintained by 100yenadmin) A live board your agent builds for you: tabs of notes, tables, charts, KPI cards and live Hermes data, in the dashboard and Hermes Desktop. It appears as a Board tab in the dashboard and a page in Desktop, and the agent lays it out with 19 native boardstate_* tools, approval widgets included. Runs a local Node >= 20 sidecar on loopback with a per-spawn nonce; no network access unless you opt in to operator-gated connectors. entries.capability_summary: browserless (community, maintained by browserless) Run Hermes' built-in browser tools on Browserless cloud browsers: stealth mode, residential proxies, captcha solving and ad blocking, with no local Chrome. One Browserless browser per task; Hermes' agent-browser daemon and CDP supervisor share it through a local CDP multiplexer, and the browser is reconnected after network drops and closed when the task ends. Disclosure — while a browser task runs, starts a background thread with a WebSocket listener on 127.0.0.1 (random port, secret path, local Host header only); connects to Browserless (production-*.browserless.io) with BROWSERLESS_TOKEN, read via get_secret; Browserless usage is metered on your plan, and residential proxy traffic costs more; no files written unless BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG is set; no telemetry. This plugin requires env var(s): BROWSERLESS_TOKEN. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6. Known issues: If the Browserless session can't start (e.g. wrong token or plan concurrency limit), Hermes falls back to a local browser; set BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG to see the reason..

entries.capability_summary: claude-subscription-directsdk (official, maintained by NousResearch) Experimental model provider that runs Hermes turns on a Claude Pro/Max subscription through the official Claude Code CLI (the Agent SDK path), so no separate API key or per-token bill. Requires the claude CLI installed and logged in; the plugin checks for it at load, in hermes model, in the pickers and before every request, and refuses cleanly with the install hint when it is missing. Disclosure — every turn is billed against your Claude subscription's Agent SDK allowance, and the provider inherits whatever account claude is logged into. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: cliproxyapi-provider (community, maintained by duu261) CLIProxyAPI as native Hermes model providers: discovers each CPA provider group (Claude, Codex, xAI, Gemini, Kiro and others) and registers one profile per group on the wire its CPA executor accepts (Anthropic Messages, Responses or Chat Completions), with context windows and reasoning levels from CPA. Disclosure — sends model-list and inference requests, authenticated with the API key env var you name, to the CPA base_url you configure; with an optional management key it also makes bounded read-only GETs to CPA's management API; with an optional billing route it sends inference, and a model-list GET, to the gateway URL you configure, authenticated with the gateway key env var you name. Known limit: Hermes strips from agent subprocesses only the key env vars a registered provider declares, so the management key env var, and on a routed instance the CPA key env var, stay readable by agent shells. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.7.

entries.capability_summary: cloudflare-web-search (community, maintained by Adolanium) Cloudflare Web Search backend for Hermes' existing web_search tool, with Ceramic, Exa, or Linkup selected in plugin settings. Search only; keep a separate extract backend. Disclosure — sends queries, result limits, gateway IDs, and optional BYOK aliases to api.cloudflare.com, which forwards searches to the selected provider and records them in AI Gateway logs. Requests can consume gateway credits or provider quota. Reads its own settings and CLOUDFLARE_WEB_SEARCH_API_TOKEN through Hermes' profile-scoped APIs. Registers one web provider, with no new tools, hooks, background processes, file writes, or self-updater. Independent community plugin. This plugin requires env var(s): CLOUDFLARE_WEB_SEARCH_API_TOKEN. Known issues: Set web.cache_enabled: false in every profile using this backend. Hermes' shared search cache omits profiles and routing settings, so repeated queries can reuse another profile's result or an earlier provider, account, gateway, or BYOK route. This setting also disables the profile's extraction result cache..

entries.capability_summary: codex-account-switch (community, maintained by SmelterLabs) Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local Hermes profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of Hermes Desktop and the gateway. Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through Hermes's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one Hermes-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json and the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment, then closes Hermes Desktop and stops and restarts the gateway once both report idle (work started in the seconds after that check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: windows. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.capability_summary: codex-truly (community, maintained by kyssta-exe) Gives ChatGPT/Codex-subscription models the context window the backend actually accepts instead of the one its catalog advertises. Measured live on 2026-10-14: gpt-6.1-sol advertises 500K, caps at 872K and accepts 919,956 input tokens, while the -900k opt-in variant had silently stopped working because Hermes only raises a legacy 272K advertisement. The plugin reads the live catalog, writes one scoped model_overrides.<provider>.<model_id>.context_window entry per model (a documented step of context resolution, so no core patch), and ships a probe that bisects the API for the true ceiling because the refusal is a late SSE event, not an HTTP error. It also selects core's Codex-backed image provider so image_generate runs on the subscription with no OPENAI_API_KEY. Disclosure - uses the profile's Codex sign-in through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: [openai-codex]); the plugin never reads auth.json and never holds a token, and network calls go only to chatgpt.com. Its only writes are scoped model_overrides entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset), through Hermes's atomic config writers; revert removes exactly what it wrote. No telemetry, no background processes, no shell commands, no self-updater. probe spends subscription quota (refused requests are free, accepted ones bill) and is never run automatically. Disclosure — uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex) and calls chatgpt.com only; its CLI and the model-callable codex_truly tool write scoped model_overrides context_window entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset) to config.yaml with no approval prompt, and `probe` sends large padding requests that spend subscription quota. This plugin registers tool(s): codex_truly. Requires Hermes >=0.21.7. Known issues: Full 1M of input is not reachable on the Codex OAuth route: ~1.05M total context is shared with a 128K output reserve, leaving ~920K of input. The plugin defaults to 900,000 and clamps to 918,000 rather than promising more.; An over-large window fails late - the request streams response.created and then returns context_length_exceeded - so it surfaces as a mid-turn crash rather than a configuration error. Lower target_context_window and re-apply if a turn dies that way..

entries.capability_summary: cognee (community, maintained by topoteretes) Knowledge-graph memory for Hermes — recall, remember, forget, and code search, backed by a local cognee server or Cognee Cloud. Disclosure — default local mode starts a detached cognee server (uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8011) plus a session-close watcher per session; turns, memory writes and indexed source go to that server and on to your configured LLM provider (OpenAI by default) or to Cognee Cloud / COGNEE_BASE_URL in remote mode; the store lives in ~/.cognee (outside HERMES_HOME, shared across profiles); cognee sends anonymous usage telemetry unless TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. This plugin registers tool(s): cognee_recall, cognee_remember, cognee_forget, cognee_switch_dataset, cognee_code_search; hook(s): on_session_end, on_memory_write.

entries.capability_summary: desensitize (community, maintained by yubingz) Chinese-context desensitization for Hermes chats. Replaces PII and business-sensitive entities — person names, company names, addresses, file paths, and magnitude figures — with reversible placeholders before a message reaches the model, then restores them in the reply. Two layers: an optional local/OpenAI-compatible LLM for semantic entity judgment, plus a sub-millisecond regex fallback (phone, ID card, email, IP, path) that keeps the conversation working when the model is unavailable. Disclosure — the semantic layer sends the pre-redaction text to the configured LLM, because recognising a name requires seeing it: with the default provider=ollama that is the local Ollama host and nothing leaves the machine, but provider=openai without an explicit base_url falls back to https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1 (remote); set base_url, or stay on ollama, to keep it local. entries.capability_summary: devin (community, maintained by Adolanium) Delegate coding tasks to the Devin CLI, on your computer or in Devin Cloud, with live progress cards and change review in Hermes Desktop. Every launch goes through Hermes approval; Cloud runs need a separate Cloud-managed-permissions confirmation. Background runs continue after the turn up to their timeout and post Devin's output back into the conversation as a message when they finish. Run history (prompts, diffs, command output) and model preferences are saved under plugin-data/devin unless persist_runs is off. Independent community add-on, not affiliated with Cognition. entries.capability_summary: devkit (community, maintained by Zek-Takai) One managed home for agent drafts: a per-session scratchpad of named buffers the agent edits in place instead of writing a new temp file per revision. Buffers live under plugin-data/devkit/, open in the Desktop code viewer, are promoted to real files only through write_file, and are removed when their chat is deleted. Disclosure — adds a short placement rule (about 120 tokens) to each turn's user message; reads state.db read-only once an hour from a background thread to find deleted chats, and also removes folders idle longer than idle_days (default 90) using its own stamps; deletes only its own folders under plugin-data/devkit/; no network calls, credentials or third-party services. This plugin registers tool(s): scratchpad; hook(s): pre_llm_call. Requires Hermes >=0.22.0. Known issues: scratchpad action=open needs the Desktop window bridge on the session gateway (NousResearch/hermes-agent#138917); on v0.22.1 open reports 'The preview pane is only available in the Hermes desktop app'. entries.capability_summary: diaktoros (community, maintained by coe0718) Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two Hermes agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended Hermes agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes, merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts, and issue-fix branches and PRs, including an opt-in auto-fix that hands issues its triage seat labels (never P0-P2, capped per day) to the fixer without a maintainer, plus an opt-in clean merge of the base into a review-only author's same-repository PR branch when it conflicts or falls behind, a branch the loop does not own; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files you provide; edits Hermes's webhook_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one hermes cron job (its migrate command replaces the old hermes-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); its backup command writes a 0600 archive of the plugin's state, including webhook route secrets, to a path you choose, and restore writes one back into the Hermes home and recreates the cron job (restore only archives you made: a crafted one can place files anywhere under the Hermes home); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices to the chat you name; deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force Hermes token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

Disclosure — Derived from hermes-live-voice by Synero (itself derived from hermes-talk) and prompt-enhance by apoapostolov (both MIT; notices preserved). Starting voice captures microphone audio. The Codex-subscription lane spawns the official codex app-server CLI under its own login with a minimal environment; through it the captured profile's SOUL.md (up to 4,000 chars), the list of installed skills and enabled tools, and Hermes task results go to OpenAI. entries.capability_summary: entropicmem (community, maintained by Ufonik88) Durable local memory for Hermes agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 34-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to HERMES_HOME/.env (append-only). entries.capability_summary: evalroute (community, maintained by keppy) Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Hermes model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "hermes evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Hermes shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run hermes -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into HERMES_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "hermes evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query hermes chat on the routed model (Nous provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a `claude -p` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except HERMES_YOLO_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from_lane, to_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max_turns value and harness name the arm ran under. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute install-encoder <dir|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "hermes evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute[encoder]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "hermes evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute (>=0.9.2,<0.10), declared as a Python dependency that Hermes installs on your confirmation. This plugin registers tool(s): evalroute_route; hook(s): pre_llm_call, pre_command, post_llm_call. Requires Hermes >=0.21.

entries.capability_summary: event-read (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with hermes cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run hermes cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar. This plugin registers tool(s): list_events, read_event; requires env var(s): CALDAV_URL, CALDAV_USER, CALDAV_PASSWORD. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.capability_summary: field-academy (community, maintained by Dgardenhire) Learn Hermes by doing real work. Four paths (Messenger, Traveler, Crossroads, Boundary Keeper) climb Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced to a capstone on a problem of your own, and a fifth, Guide, covers setting Hermes up for a client: practice labs built from made-up data, a proposal, one real service run by a scheduled job for several days, a recovery drill, and a review signed by a reviewer you choose. Every mission ends with a check on something you made; your own Hermes scores your written answers in a new chat; passed missions come back for short spaced reviews; and at the end of a path you can create a Field Record, your own self-issued learning record. Field Academy is an independent community plugin. It is not made, issued or endorsed by Nous Research. Disclosure — no network calls (a source link opens in your browser only when you click it); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers six tools, two hooks, the /academy command and one skill: pre_llm_call may add one sentence offering a practice to the user message, only in interactive desktop, TUI and CLI sessions, and post_tool_call records which tool was used; pressing Try it or a scoring button opens a new chat and sends the practice or scoring prompt there (on an older Hermes it goes to the clipboard instead); the Desktop page calls gateway list methods only (session.list, cron.manage list, skills.manage list, tools.list, mcp.catalog, commands.catalog, setup.runtime_check); stores progress, pasted documents, practice labs, review packets and saved Field Records in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/field-academy/; reads a file you name (UTF-8 text, max 5 MiB) and hashes a recording you name without copying it; Guide labs write and check made-up .env and auth.json files inside its own labs folder (refusing to build in a real Hermes home) and never read Hermes's real ones; on the Guide path reads Hermes's run-history database read-only and immutable, jobs.json and up to 25 log files (2 MiB each), keeping only timestamps for the job you name, and reads install-stamp.json for the Hermes version; no private Hermes imports. This plugin registers tool(s): field_academy_snapshot, field_academy_mission, field_academy_grade_explanation, field_academy_grade_review, field_academy_grade_deployer, field_academy_record_evidence; hook(s): post_tool_call, pre_llm_call. Requires Hermes >=0.22.0.

entries.capability_summary: fish-audio (community, maintained by 100yenadmin) The official Fish Audio plugin, maintained by Electric Sheep: expressive text-to-speech in 80+ languages, including Fish's Drama 3 model with word-level direction, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in Hermes Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a Hermes speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop, and live dictation captions on Hermes 0.21.6+ (stt.streaming: true). Adds the fish_speak, fish_voices and fish_transcribe tools, /fish and hermes fish commands, and three skills. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to api.fish.audio's realtime speech-to-text endpoint while you speak, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model, whose requests Fish may use to improve its models. The key comes from the profile's secret scope (Hermes stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH_API_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to Hermes's audio cache; clone samples and recordings it uploads must be regular audio files, and Hermes config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through Hermes's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Hermes dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through Hermes's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page and /fish alias can set or reset the profile's Fish model and voice and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. No telemetry. This plugin registers tool(s): fish_speak, fish_voices, fish_transcribe; hook(s): transform_llm_output, pre_tool_call; requires env var(s): FISH_API_KEY. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6. Known issues: Hermes's text normaliser alters <|speaker:N|> markup and Drama 3 closing tags such as </whisper> on the plain text_to_speech path; use fish_speak for multi-speaker speech and Drama 3 word tags (NousResearch/hermes-agent#133131).; Under plugins.isolation: host the hermes fish terminal command is unavailable and voice replies use whole-file speech instead of streaming; /fish, the tools and both providers still work..

The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Hermes dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through Hermes's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page and /fish alias can set or reset the profile's Fish model and voice and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. No telemetry.
known_issues: Hermes's text normaliser alters <|speaker:N|> markup and Drama 3 closing tags such as </whisper> on the plain text_to_speech path; use fish_speak for multi-speaker speech and Drama 3 word tags (NousResearch/hermes-agent#133131).
Under plugins.isolation: host the hermes fish terminal command is unavailable and voice replies use whole-file speech instead of streaming; /fish, the tools and both providers still work.

entries.capability_summary: gbrain-pointer (community, maintained by praggybuilds) Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry. This plugin requires env var(s): GBRAIN_MCP_CLIENT_ID, GBRAIN_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.capability_summary: git-autosave (community, maintained by xiaoyaner0201) Lightweight local alternative to directory checkpoints for Git projects. Before a mutating tool call it saves the affected repository's working state to a private local shadow ref (refs/hermes-autosave/<branch>, with reflog) through a private index, or copies the single existing file outside Git; `hermes autosave find` and `restore` recover a pre-edit version. Disclosure — runs local git subprocesses in repositories the agent touches (hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor and lazy fetch disabled); writes shadow refs/reflogs into those repositories' .git and unencrypted file copies into its plugin-data directory; never changes HEAD, branches, the real index or the working tree and never pushes; skips credential stores (.env, auth.json, .ssh, .aws, .docker, .kube, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and dependency directories; `hermes autosave sweep` reads the session database read-only and is scheduled by the user; no network, no background processes; it observes only and never blocks or approves a tool call. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.22.0. Known issues: One V4A patch that moves a symlink and then updates the moved path can miss the edited file on case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems; commit first or send the Move and the Update as separate calls..

Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. A branch whose direct push the remote refuses on policy grounds (branch protection, a PR-required ruleset) is never committed to again: the hook drops its own unpushed commit, leaves the edit staged and dirty, and reports it once. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, post_llm_call, on_session_end.

entries.capability_summary: github_app (community, maintained by himanusia) GitHub and GitHub Enterprise tools with bot-first attribution and approval-gated issue/PR writes.
